Description: Server Components render on the server with zero client JS by default; use them unless you need interactivity
Do: Keep components as Server Components unless they use state events or browser APIs
Don't: Add 'use client' to every component by default
Code Good: async function Page() { const data = await db.query(); return <List data={data} /> }
Code Bad: 'use client'; export default function Page() { useEffect(() => db.query()) }

Description: Only components that need hooks or event handlers need 'use client'; keep the boundary as low as possible
Do: Add 'use client' only to the leaf component that requires it
Don't: Put 'use client' on layout files or high in the tree
Code Good: 'use client'; export function LikeButton() { const [liked] = useState(false) }
Code Bad: 'use client'; export default function Layout({ children }) { }

Guideline: Colocate related files in the route folder
Description: App Router supports colocating components tests and utilities inside route segments
Do: Keep page-specific components inside the route folder
Don't: Put all components in a global /components directory regardless of scope
Code Good: app/dashboard/page.tsx + app/dashboard/DashboardChart.tsx
Code Bad: app/components/DashboardChart.tsx used only by dashboard

Description: Layouts persist across navigations and avoid re-mounting shared UI like sidebars
Do: Shared chrome in layout.tsx; page-specific UI in page.tsx
Don't: Re-render nav and sidebar inside every page component
Code Good: app/layout.tsx wraps all pages with <Nav /> and <Footer />
Code Bad: Each page renders its own <Nav /> and <Footer />

Description: Fetch directly in async Server Components to eliminate client waterfalls
Do: async/await in Server Components for data dependencies
Don't: Client-side fetch in useEffect for data that can be server-rendered
Code Good: async function Page() { const posts = await fetchPosts(); return <Posts data={posts} /> }
Code Bad: useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/posts').then(setPosts) } [])

Description: Next.js extends fetch with cache and revalidation controls baked in
Do: fetch(url { cache: 'force-cache' }) for static data; { next: { revalidate: 60 } } for ISR
Don't: Always use no-store or always force-cache without considering the use case
Code Good: fetch(url { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
Code Bad: fetch(url { cache: 'no-store' }) for static marketing content

Description: Await independent data fetches concurrently to reduce total latency
Do: Promise.all for independent server fetches
Don't: Sequential await chains for unrelated data
Code Good: const [user posts] = await Promise.all([getUser() getPosts()])
Code Bad: const user = await getUser(); const posts = await getPosts();

Description: Runtime validation catches API shape mismatches before they cause render errors
Do: Validate API responses with Zod before using them
Don't: Trust external API shapes without validation
Code Good: const user = UserSchema.parse(await fetchUser())
Code Bad: const user = await fetchUser() as User

Description: loading.tsx automatically wraps the page in a Suspense boundary for instant shell
Do: Add loading.tsx next to page.tsx for routes with server data
Don't: Leave routes without any loading state
Code Good: app/dashboard/loading.tsx exports a <DashboardSkeleton />
Code Bad: No loading.tsx; user sees blank page during fetch

Guideline: Add error.tsx for route error handling
Description: error.tsx catches runtime errors in a route segment and shows a recovery UI
Do: Error.tsx with a retry button in every major route segment
Don't: Let route errors bubble to a top-level crash
Code Good: app/dashboard/error.tsx exports <ErrorFallback reset={reset} />
Code Bad: No error.tsx; one bad fetch crashes the whole app

Guideline: Use generateStaticParams for dynamic static routes
Description: Pre-render known dynamic segments at build time for maximum performance
Do: generateStaticParams to statically generate [slug] pages
Don't: Skip generateStaticParams and always render dynamic pages on request
Code Good: export async function generateStaticParams() { return posts.map(p => ({ slug: p.slug })) }
Code Bad: Dynamic page with no generateStaticParams that could be static

Guideline: Use notFound() and redirect() from next/navigation
Description: Declarative server-side redirects and 404s are cleaner than throwing errors
Do: notFound() when a resource is missing; redirect() for auth guards
Don't: Return empty UI or throw generic errors for missing resources
Code Good: if (!user) notFound();
Code Bad:
if (!user) return

Not found

Description: The Image component auto-resizes lazy-loads and serves modern formats like WebP
Do: next/image for every raster image with width and height set
Don't: tags for local or remote images in Next.js apps
Code Good: <Image src={hero} alt="Hero" width={1200} height={600} priority />

Description: next/font self-hosts fonts at build time eliminating layout shift and extra round trips
Do: next/font/google for Google Fonts and next/font/local for custom fonts
Don't: @import Google Fonts in CSS or link tag in head
Code Good: const inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] })
Code Bad: <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/..." rel="stylesheet" />

Guideline: Dynamic import for heavy Client Components
Description: Dynamically importing large client-side bundles keeps the initial JS payload small
Do: dynamic(() => import('./HeavyEditor') { ssr: false }) for browser-only heavy UI
Don't: Import chart and editor libraries statically in the Client Component root
Code Good: const Editor = dynamic(() => import('./Editor') { ssr: false })
Code Bad: import Editor from './Editor' at the top of a route file

Description: Static metadata improves SEO and is free for Server Components
Do: Export a metadata object or generateMetadata in every page.tsx
Don't: Leave metadata undefined or set it only on the root layout
Code Good: export const metadata = { title: 'Dashboard' description: 'User dashboard' }
Code Bad: No metadata export in page.tsx

Description: Server Actions run on the server and can be called directly from forms or clients
Do: Server Actions for form submissions and data mutations
Don't: API routes for simple mutations that don't need streaming
Code Good: async function createPost(formData: FormData) { 'use server'; await db.create(...) }
Code Bad: fetch('/api/posts' { method: 'POST' body: formData })

Description: Server Actions are HTTP endpoints; never trust input from the client
Do: Zod-validate all Server Action arguments before writing to the database
Don't: Trust FormData or arguments passed to a Server Action
Code Good: const parsed = schema.safeParse(Object.fromEntries(formData));
Code Bad: await db.insert({ title: formData.get('title') }) without validation

Description: After a mutation call revalidatePath or revalidateTag to keep pages fresh
Do: revalidatePath or revalidateTag at the end of every mutating Server Action
Don't: Forget to revalidate and leave users seeing stale data
Code Good: revalidatePath('/dashboard'); redirect('/dashboard');
Code Bad: return { success: true } without revalidating any cached data

Guideline: Add optimistic updates for perceived speed
Description: Update the UI immediately and reconcile with the server response for fast UX
Do: useOptimistic for list items that are created or toggled
Don't: Wait for the server round-trip before showing any UI change
Code Good: const [optimisticPosts addOptimistic] = useOptimistic(posts)
Code Bad: await createPost(data); // UI freezes until server responds

Description: Next.js caches at request memoization Data Cache Full Route Cache and Router Cache levels
Do: Read the caching docs; opt out selectively with noStore() or dynamic = 'force-dynamic'
Don't: Default to no-store everywhere out of fear of stale data
Code Good: import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache'; noStore();
Code Bad: export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' on every page

Description: Tagging allows surgical cache invalidation without revalidating unrelated data
Do: fetch(url { next: { tags: ['posts'] } }) and revalidateTag('posts') after mutation
Don't: Use time-based revalidation when event-based is more accurate
Code Good: fetch(url { next: { tags: ['user-123'] } })
Code Bad: revalidatePath('/') after every mutation

Description: Cache database queries ORM calls and any async work that isn't a fetch
Do: unstable_cache wrapping db queries with tags and revalidation period
Don't: Re-query the database on every request for data that rarely changes
Code Good: const getUser = unstable_cache(async (id) => db.find(id) ['user'] { revalidate: 60 })
Code Bad: async function getUser(id) { return db.find(id) } called on every render

Guideline: Mark pages dynamic only when truly needed
Description: Dynamic rendering disables all page-level caching; use it only for user-specific data
Do: Keep pages static or ISR; use dynamic = 'force-dynamic' only when cookies or headers are required
Don't: Add export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' as a default to all pages
Code Good: export const revalidate = 3600; // ISR for mostly-static content
Code Bad: export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' on a marketing page

Description: Public vars must have NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix; secret vars must never go to the client
Do: NEXT_PUBLIC_ only for values safe to expose; keep secrets server-only
Don't: Expose API keys in NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables
Code Good: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL for client use; DATABASE_URL server-only
Code Bad: NEXT_PUBLIC_DATABASE_URL='postgres://...'

Guideline: Use Edge Runtime for latency-sensitive routes
Description: Edge Runtime runs at CDN nodes with sub-10ms cold starts; ideal for auth and redirects
Do: Edge Runtime for middleware and simple API routes close to users
Don't: Run heavy Node.js-only code on the Edge Runtime
Code Good: export const runtime = 'edge'; // in a lightweight API route
Code Bad: export const runtime = 'edge' in a route that requires fs or native modules

Description: Streaming sends HTML progressively so users see content before all data is ready
Do: Wrap slow data-fetching components in <Suspense> to stream them independently
Don't: Await all data before sending any HTML to the browser
Code Good: <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}><SlowFeed /></Suspense>
Code Bad: await all data at the top of the page before returning any JSX

Description: Server-side metadata generation ensures crawlers see correct titles and OG tags
Do: Export generateMetadata as an async function when metadata depends on route params
Don't: Set a single static title in the root layout for all pages
Code Good: async function generateMetadata({ params }) { return { title: post.title } }
Code Bad: export const metadata = { title: 'My App' } as the only metadata

Description: A machine-generated sitemap stays up to date and improves crawl coverage
Do: app/sitemap.ts that returns all public URLs
Don't: Manually maintain a static sitemap.xml or skip it entirely
Code Good: export default async function sitemap() { return posts.map(p => ({ url: p.url })) }
Code Bad: No sitemap.ts or a static sitemap that misses new pages

Description: A programmatic robots file lets you block staging environments and private routes
Do: app/robots.ts that checks the environment and disallows private paths
Don't: No robots.txt letting crawlers index staging or admin routes
Code Good: export default function robots() { return { rules: { userAgent: '*' allow: '/' } } }
Code Bad: No robots.ts; staging site indexed by Google

Description: Next.js can generate OG images at build or request time via the Image Response API
Do: app/opengraph-image.tsx using ImageResponse for dynamic per-page OG images
Don't: Use a single static OG image for all pages including dynamic content
Code Good: export default function OGImage({ params }) { return new ImageResponse(...) }
Code Bad: <meta property="og:image" content="/og.png" /> same image for all pages
